newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Bidders for Kazakh telcoms monopoly cut to three.
newsitem.headline: Bidders for Kazakh telcoms monopoly cut to three.

text.p: The number of bidders for a 40 percent stake in NAK Kazakhtelekom, Kazakhstan's state-owned telecoms monopoly, has been narrowed to three, a privatisation source said on Monday.

The source said of the seven companies that took part in the tender, only Malaysia's Usaha Tegas Sdn Bnd, Korea's Daewoo and Kaztel Investment Group, registered in the Virgin Islands, were still competing.
Germany's Siemens AG, Alcatel Alstrom SA unit Alcatel Sel AG, Korea's Hanwha and Kazakhstan Asset Management Ltd have dropped out.
The tender was announced in January after an earlier deal with Germany's Deutsche Telekom AG fell through in December.
The monopoly wants an investor to share responsibility for debts of 420 million marks for a credit made in 1992 by Germany's investment agency Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau, to be repaid by 2004.
Looking for investment worth over one billion marks, Kazakhtelekom aims to increase telephone lines for the ex-Soviet state's 16.9 million population to five million from the existing 2.1 million.
